explanation.text:
(Pro. 15:1-33)

soft--tender or gentle.

turneth . . . wrath--from any one.

stir up--as a smouldering fire is excited.

bsb.text: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.

explanation.text:
useth . . . aright--commends knowledge by its proper use.

poureth out--utters abundantly (Pro 12:23), and so disgusts others.

bsb.text: The tongue of the wise commends knowledge, but the mouth of the fool spouts folly.

explanation.text: beholding--watching (compare Pro 5:21; Psa 66:7).

bsb.text: The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good.

explanation.text:
A wholesome tongue--(Compare Margin), pacifying and soothing language.

tree of life-- (Pro 3:18; Pro 11:30).

perverseness therein--cross, ill-natured language.

breach . . . spirit--(compare Isa 65:14, Hebrew), grieves, instead of appeasing.

bsb.text: A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but a perverse tongue crushes the spirit.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 4:1; Pro 10:17; Pro. 13:1-18).

is prudent--acts discreetly.

bsb.text: A fool rejects his father’s discipline, but whoever heeds correction is prudent.

explanation.text:
treasure--implying utility.

trouble--vexation and affliction.

bsb.text: The house of the righteous has great treasure, but the income of the wicked is trouble.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:20-21).

heart . . . not so--not right, or vain.

bsb.text: The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools.

explanation.text:
The sacrifice [and] prayer--are acts of worship.

way . . . followeth . . . righteousness--denote conduct. God's regard for the worship and deeds of the righteous and wicked respectively, so stated in Psa 50:17; Isa 1:11.

bsb.text: The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight.

explanation.text:
The way of the wicked is an abomination unto the Lord,.... The way his heart devises, which he chooses and delights in, in which he walks; nor will he leave it, nor can he be diverted from it, but by the powerful grace of God. This is a way not good, but evil, and so an abomination to the Lord; and the whole tenor and course of his life, which is meant by his way being evil: hence his sacrifices, and all his external duties of religion performed by him, are abominable to the Lord; for, while he continues in a course of sin, all his religious exercises will be of no avail, cannot be pleasing and acceptable to God;

but he loveth him that followeth after righteousness; either after a justifying righteousness; not the righteousness of the law, which the carnal Jews followed after, but did not attain unto; nor is righteousness to be had by the works of the law, nor any justification by it, nor can a man be acceptable to God on account of it; but the righteousness of Christ, which he has wrought out, and is revealed in the Gospel: to follow after this supposes a want of one; a sense of that want; a view of the glory, fulness, suitableness, and excellency of Christ's righteousness; an eager desire after it, sometimes expressed by hungering and thirsting after it, as here by a pursuit of it; which means no other than an earnest and importunate request to be found in it: and such, as they shall be satisfied or filled with it, so they are loved by the Lord, and are acceptable to him through the righteousness they are seeking after: or else it may be understood of following after true holiness of heart and life, without which there is no seeing the Lord; and though perfection in it is not attainable in this live, yet a gracious soul presses after it, which is well pleasing in the sight of God.

bsb.text: The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:17).

the way--that in which God would have him to go (Pro 2:13; Psa 119:1).

bsb.text: Discipline is harsh for him who leaves the path; he who hates correction will die.

explanation.text:
Hell-- (Psa 16:10).

destruction--or, "Abaddon," the place of the destroyer. All the unseen world is open to God, much more men's hearts.

bsb.text: Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD—how much more the hearts of men!

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 9:8).

go unto the wise--to be instructed.

bsb.text: A mocker does not love to be reproved, nor will he consult the wise.

explanation.text:
maketh . . . countenance--or, "benefits the countenance."

spirit is broken--and so the countenance is sad.

bsb.text: A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance, but sorrow of the heart crushes the spirit.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 10:21-22). The wise grow wiser, the fools more foolish (Pro 9:9).

bsb.text: A discerning heart seeks knowledge, but the mouth of a fool feeds on folly.

explanation.text:
The state of the heart governs the outward condition.

evil--sad, contrasted with the cheerfulness of a feast.

bsb.text: All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast.

explanation.text: trouble--agitation, implying the anxieties and perplexities attending wealth held by worldlings (Pro 16:18; Ti1 6:6).

bsb.text: Better a little with the fear of the LORD than great treasure with turmoil.

explanation.text:
dinner--or, "allowance" (Kg2 25:30) --

of herbs--and that the plainest.

and hatred--(compare Pro 10:12, Pro 10:18).

bsb.text: Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 14:29; Pro 16:32).

bsb.text: A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute.

explanation.text:
The difficulties of the slothful result from want of energy; the righteous find a

plain [and open] way--literally, "a highway," by diligence (Sa1 10:7; Psa 1:3).

bsb.text: The way of the slacker is like a hedge of thorns, but the path of the upright is a highway.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 10:1).

bsb.text: A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother.

explanation.text: walketh uprightly--and so finds his joy (Pro 3:6; Pro 10:23).

bsb.text: Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment, but a man of understanding walks a straight path.

explanation.text: Without counsel--or, "deliberation," implying a wise deference to the opinions of the wise and good, contrasted with rashness.

bsb.text: Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed.

explanation.text: Good advice blesses the giver and receiver.

bsb.text: A man takes joy in a fitting reply—and how good is a timely word!

explanation.text: (Compare Col 3:2). Holy purposes prevent sinning, and so its evils.

bsb.text: The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol.

explanation.text:
The most desolate who have God's aid have more permanent good than the self-reliant sinner (Pro 2:22; Pro 12:7).

border--or, "boundary for possessions" (Psa 78:54).

bsb.text: The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow.

explanation.text: are pleasant words--that is, pleasing to God (Pro 8:8-9).

bsb.text: The LORD detests the thoughts of the wicked, but the words of the pure are pleasant to Him.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 11:17). Avarice brings trouble to him and his.

hateth gifts--or, "bribes" (Exo 23:8; Psa 15:5), and is not avaricious.

bsb.text: He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household, but he who hates bribes will live.

explanation.text: (Compare Pro 15:14; Pro 10:11). Caution is the fruit of wisdom; rashness of folly.

bsb.text: The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil.

explanation.text: far . . . wicked--in His love and favor (Psa 22:11; Psa 119:155).

bsb.text: The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous.

explanation.text:
light of the eyes-- (Pro 13:9). What gives light rejoiceth the heart, by relieving from anxiety as to our course; so

good report--or, "doctrine" (Isa 28:9; Isa 53:1),

maketh . . . fat--or, "gives prosperity" (Pro 3:13-17; Pro 9:11). The last clause is illustrated by the first.

bsb.text: The light of the eyes cheers the heart, and good news nourishes the bones.

explanation.text:
(Compare Pro 10:17).

reproof of life--which leads to life.

abideth . . . wise--is numbered among them.

bsb.text: He who listens to life-giving reproof will dwell among the wise.

explanation.text:
refuseth--or, "neglects," "passes by" (Pro 1:25; Pro 4:15).

despiseth . . . soul--so acts as if esteeming its interests of no value.

bsb.text: He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding.

explanation.text:
The fear . . . wisdom--Wisdom instructs in true piety.

before . . . humility--(compare Luk 24:26; Pe1 1:11); opposite (compare Pro 16:18).

Next: Proverbs Chapter 16

bsb.text: The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor.
